### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 45 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b068f346a1de395c18a39ca3e28e6d4d787bf927` — the merge of head `90e185aa5bc64a04b7cdf4f047c7bd1e31a11afa` into base `9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b068f346a1de395c18a39ca3e28e6d4d787bf927 && git checkout b068f346a1de395c18a39ca3e28e6d4d787bf927
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2 90e185aa5bc64a04b7cdf4f047c7bd1e31a11afa && git checkout -B drift-repro 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2 && git merge --no-ff 90e185aa5bc64a04b7cdf4f047c7bd1e31a11afa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `90e185aa5bc64a04b7cdf4f047c7bd1e31a11afa`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: brief 6980194000; card #35138 (claim 6975089907, claim amendment 3 6978597356, os-dev report 6980131954 and area note 6980179875); card #35144 (every comment, among them the hand-on 6977042103 and the seat ruling 6978086158); PR #35193 (body and the `mcp-http-tools.ts` on its head `f766f5dcc0`); PR #35202 (body and comments); the full diff against merge-base `ba6556c617` (3 files, +383/−7, 2 commits); the changeset; and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at `origin/main` only. `origin/main` has 2 commits since the merge-base, and neither touches `packages/mcp`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` or `packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts`.

Face: the committed file list is `.changeset/mcp-aggregate-lookup-group-labels.md`, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` and `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.aggregation-entry.test.ts`. It touches no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path. `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` decides no face from the paths and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries `yes (widening)`. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` succeeded on this head. So this is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, with no ④. Every file is inside the file surface of amendment 3, and `stdio-data-bridge.ts` was not needed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **CI on this head is still running.** 52 check-runs: 30 success, 16 skipped, 6 in progress, 0 failure. Still running: `Test Core` shards 1 to 6 of 10. Complete and green: `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, every `Type Check ·` lane, every `Lint ·` lane (among them `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, which carries the NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`), `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core` shards 7 to 10, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`. I judge on what is complete. The seat must see the 6 running shards finish green on this head before landing.
- **One handler, both doors: right.** `aggregate_records` is registered once, in `registerObjectTools`, which the HTTP door and the stdio door both call. The name read is `bridge.query` on the same bridge object the aggregate used. On the HTTP door that is the per-request bridge with the request's context (`callData('query', ...)` at `origin/main`). On the stdio door it is `resolvePrincipal()` and `engine.find` with that context, after the same exposure gates `query_records` passes. The stdio pin drives the real stdio bridge through a real MCP client and checks the engine read is one `find` with the principal's own context.
- **When a key is a lookup key, and the member's name: right.** A key counts only when the caller's served schema shows it as `lookup` or `master_detail` with a non-empty `reference`. A date-bucketed key is skipped, and a field the served view does not show is skipped. The member is KEY__label, where KEY is the group column: the alias when the call gives one, else the field name. It is inserted right after its key, so the order of the existing columns does not change. A column the aggregate already answers under that name is never overwritten (unpinned: N3).
- **The read: as the caller, batched, after the cap: right.** Labels are read only for `served`, the slice after `maxLimit`, so `truncated` and `totalGroups` are computed exactly as before. Keys that reference the same object are grouped, and their ids (deduplicated, non-empty strings only) go into one `bridge.query` per referenced object: `where: { id: { $in: ids } }`, `fields: ['id', NAME_FIELD]`, `limit: ids.length`. The batched-read pin covers 60 groups with a cap of 50 and two keys on one object: one read, 52 ids, no id from past the cap. The name field is `resolveDisplayField` (ADR-0079) over the referenced object as the caller is served it. If that pointer names a field the served view does not show, no labels are added for that object. The code does not fall back to another field.
- **Present only for a returned record with a non-blank name: right, at rule level.** A label is set only for an id the caller's read returns, where that id was asked for and the name is a non-blank string or a finite number. Every other key, including a null key, keeps exactly the columns it had. So the answer is built only from what the caller's own read returns, and a record the caller cannot read gives the same answer as one that no longer exists. The CONTROL compares the two answers whole and as JSON text. The dev's ablation note is right: the comparison half cannot be turned red from inside the handler, because the handler sees only the read's answer. That is the rule working as designed.
- **Nothing added when the name cannot be read: right.** No label is added, and no read is made, when the bridge has no `servedObjectDefinitionOf`, when the lookup field, the referenced object or its name field is not served, or when the referenced object fails the read tools' `readGuard` (a `sys_` object without the AI-read opt-in). A read that throws, or answers no `records` list, is caught and adds nothing. A name read never fails the aggregate. The CONTROLs pin each of these with the answer compared whole. `servedFieldsOf` is split into `servedDefinitionOf` and `fieldMapOf` with the same result for every input: no member, a null answer, a throw and a non-map `fields` all still give `undefined`.
- **Tool description: right, with N1.** Three sentences are added. They say a lookup or master-detail group carries the label beside the record id, read with the caller's own permissions; tell the model to name such a group by its label and never by the id; and tell it to say that a group with no label cannot be named. This matches the code. For a null key, the wording is looser than it should be (N1).
- **Built entry of `@objectstack/mcp`: nothing removed, renamed or narrowed.** The `exports` map is unchanged. No `export` line is added or removed. The two new functions, the two new constants and the two split-out helpers are module-private. `resolveDisplayField` comes from `@objectstack/spec/data`, which already exports `display-name` and is already a `workspace:*` dependency. The answer is untyped JSON text with no output schema in `packages/spec`. `rows`, `totalGroups`, `truncated` and `currencies` keep their names, their meaning and the conditions under which they appear. The only change to `rows` is the new member that appears only when it has a value. No input accepted before is now refused.
- **SQL push-down: no finding, the second read is reasoned.** This adds an in-app id collection and a second read, which is a finding unless a reason is given. Here it is reasoned. Amendment 3's rule asks for the name as the caller's own read of the referenced object, so that object's own object, field and record permissions apply to the name. The aggregate itself stays one database GROUP BY. The name read is one statement per referenced object. Its `$in` runs in the database, and it is bounded by the cap (at most 50 ids per key by default). It is the same read shape `delete_records` uses for an id list.

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix): the merge carry to #35193 is not written where its dev reads it.** Area note 6980179875 says whichever of #35202 and #35193 merges `main` second must label the cut path's served rows the same way, while the default path keeps `groups`, `totalGroups` and the labels. #35193's head has a separate cut-path return (`answer.totalGroups`, before the default path). Neither its body nor any comment on #35193 or #35144 after the 12:07Z ruling mentions labels. If #35193 merges second, a textual merge that keeps both insertions labels only the default path. The cut path would then answer lookup groups with no label, and the new description tells the model those records cannot be named. That gives a wrong answer on every call that sends an order and a limit. To close it, post one comment on #35144 (or #35193) giving the carry from the area note. No change to this head is needed. The original reviewer reads that comment as the delta.
- **N1 (nit): the description's no-label sentence does not set the null group apart.** "Where a group has no __label, its record cannot be named" also covers the group whose key is null, which has no record. A model may describe the empty bucket ("no account") as a record that cannot be named. Adding "a group with a null key has no record" to the clause would close it. The rows are correct, so this has no correctness or contract effect.
- **N2 (nit): the PR body's #35193 note still says the default path keeps `groupCount`.** Area note 6980179875 corrects it: the published name stays `totalGroups` and `groupCount` is not added, and #35193's head already has no `groupCount`. Prose only. Fix it if the body is edited for any other reason.
- **N3 (nit): the never-overwrite rule has no pin.** The code keeps a column the aggregate already answers as KEY__label (an aggregation alias spelled that way), and the PR body states the rule. No test sets such an alias, and no ablation removes the check. The code is right today.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/mcp-aggregate-lookup-group-labels.md`: right.** It bumps `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch`. That is the only published package whose source changes, and the test file is not published. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 says that `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and that a widening outside the protocol also ships as `patch`. CI `Check Changeset` succeeded on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: right.** It starts its line in both the PR body and the changeset, and the arm is from the closed pair. A new answer member that is present only when it has a value is a widening. Nothing is removed, renamed or newly refused. Claim 6975089907 and amendment 3 declared `Clause-②: yes`.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No spec key, accepted value or metadata type is added. The code reads the existing `reference`, `nameField` and `displayNameField` keys with their declared meaning, and no guidance text enters the spec (ADR-0149 M1).
- **Changeset prose against the diff: right.**
  - "groups by a `lookup` or `master_detail` field ... a new member ... beside the key": true (①).
  - "from the referenced object's name field (`nameField`, as ADR-0079 resolves it)": `resolveDisplayField` over the served definition.
  - "the key's alias when the call gives one": true, and pinned.
  - "The same spelling is used by the hosted ask tools": read from amendment 3 (cloud#4795). It is not checked in this repo.
  - "on both the HTTP and the stdio door": one handler, two bridges (①).
  - "read as the caller, through the same bridge and context as the aggregate, in one batched read of the referenced object for the groups the tool serves": true, and pinned on both the recording bridge and the stdio bridge.
  - "A label is present only for a key whose record the caller's read returns with a non-blank name. Any other key carries no label, and nothing else in the answer changes": true.
  - "No label is added, and the answer is exactly as before, when ... not served ... a system object the tool does not read, or when the read fails. A failed name read never fails the aggregate": true, and pinned.
  - "Existing members (`rows`, `totalGroups`, `truncated`, `currencies`) are unchanged": true for their names and meaning. The new member inside `rows` is the stated change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open questions: none in the report.
- Deviation, two single-file vitest runs outside the verify lock: process only. Every package run and every ablation ran under it. Accepted in 6980179875.
- Deviation, model-free commit trailers and the AGENTS.md footer form: process only.
- Deviation, `test:repo` left to CI: answered. No repo-project test is touched. CI `Test Core` carries it, and 6 of its shards are still running (①).
- NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: answered. CI `Lint · repo & tooling gates` carries it, and it succeeded on this head.
- The #35193 merge note: answered by area note 6980179875 (`totalGroups`, no `groupCount`). It is not yet written on the carrier's card or PR: S1. The PR body still carries the old wording: N2.
- `security_findings: none`: I agree. Nothing in this diff reads with rights the caller does not have.
- Ablations A to F2: each mutation landed and turned the pin file red, and each was restored to the HEAD blob `a3381bff9791`, the blob this head carries for `mcp-http-tools.ts`. The ablation limit on the unreadable-versus-deleted comparison is accepted (①). No ablation covers the date-bucket skip (one token, stated in the jsdoc) or the never-overwrite check (N3).
- Docs: `content/docs/ai/natural-language-queries.mdx` and `connect-mcp.mdx` name `aggregate_records` but do not list its result members. The sentence "It does not join across objects" stays true of the GROUP BY. No page becomes untrue, and no page is owed. `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md` does not teach the label. The tool description carries it, so a skill sentence would be a follow-up, not owed here.
- Process notes: the PR is a draft. Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay), assignee `os-warren`, so no extra author note is owed. S1 is closed by a comment on #35144 or #35193, with no new head. Before landing, the seat must see the 6 running `Test Core` shards finish green on the final head (①).

### L1 review (#35138, PR 4) · 2026-11-18T13:59Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: 90e185aa5bc64a04b7cdf4f047c7bd1e31a11afa
Read: the full diff at this head against merge base ba6556c617 (3 files, +383/−7), with claim amendment 3 6978597356, contract record 6980323967 and its delta 6980364931, and the carry note 6980343159 on #35144.

**Fixes vs Part of.** This is PR 4 of the W0 plan. The body says `Refs #35138`, and no closing keyword appears in the body or the changeset, so a merge does not close #35138. As on #35185 and #35186, the checklist's form is `Part of`, and `Refs` has the same effect.

**Claim file surface.** Amendment 3 gives PR 4 three things: `mcp-http-tools.ts` (the `aggregate_records` handler, its module-private helpers and its description), its tests, and one changeset. The diff is exactly that. `servedFieldsOf` is split into `servedDefinitionOf` and `fieldMapOf`, both module-private and with the same behaviour. `stdio-data-bridge.ts` is not touched, because the stdio door reads the name through its existing `query` and `servedObjectDefinitionOf`.

**Each changeset sentence against the diff.** The changeset is new and is not on `main`. It bumps `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch`.
- *"`lookup` or `master_detail` … `<key>__label` … the alias when the call gives one":* `LOOKUP_GROUP_TYPES` holds the two types, and a key needs a served field with a non-empty `reference`. A date-bucketed key is skipped. The column is the alias, else the field.
- *"The referenced object's name field (ADR-0079)":* `resolveDisplayField` reads the served definition of the target, and the name field must itself be served.
- *"Read as the caller … one batched read … for the groups served":*
  - It runs after the cut, over `served` only.
  - It makes one `bridge.query(target, { where: { id: { $in: ids } }, fields: ['id', nameField], limit: ids.length })` per referenced object, through the same bridge, so the caller's object, field and record rules apply.
  - The target first passes the tool's own `readGuard`.
- *"Present only for a key whose record the caller's read returns with a non-blank name":* names are kept only for asked ids, as a non-blank string or a finite number. A missing record and an unreadable one leave the same absence, so the answer never says which. A column the aggregate itself answers as `<key>__label` is never overwritten.
- *"No label … the answer exactly as before … a failed name read never fails the aggregate":* in `recordNamesAsCaller`, every exit is `undefined` inside a `try`. An unserved target, name field or lookup field, a refused system object, a throw, and a non-`records` answer each return the rows unchanged.
- *"The tool description now tells a model …":* the three sentences are added as stated.
- *"Existing members unchanged":* `rows` now carries the labelled copies, and `totalGroups`, `truncated` and `currencies` are unchanged.

**Tests.** The aggregation-entry file has 8 new cases.
- Lookup and master-detail labels by key and by alias.
- CONTROL cases: a non-lookup key that holds a record id, an unreturned or deleted record, a blank name and a null key, the unserved target, name field or lookup field and the system object, and a read that throws or answers no list.
- The one batched read as the caller, for served groups only.
- The stdio door under the caller's own context.

**Clause-②: yes (widening).** TIER_DEFAULT record 6980323967 is PASS on this same head. Delta 6980364931 closes S1 through 6980343159, the carry to #35193: the cut path labels its served rows through the same helper. N1 to N3 stay nits.

**Governance.** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35202`: NOT governed, 0 of 3 paths on the register, 390 changed lines.

**CI at this head**, from check-runs: 37 success and 16 skipped, with none failed or in progress (all ten `Test Core` shards included). The PR is mergeable `clean`.

#### Must-fix
None.

#### Should-fix
None.

#### Notes
- **N1, read cost.** The name read goes through `bridge.query` with a `limit`. Since #35185 the stdio bridge counts every paged read, and the HTTP door's `findData` counts too. So each labelled call adds one name read plus one count per referenced object, for at most `maxLimit` ids. That is bounded, and I add no ask.
- **N2, merge order with #35193.** Whichever of #35193 and this PR merges `main` second owes the cut-path labels and a pin (6980343159). If that is this PR, the merge comes back to me as a delta.
